Definition: Incurred losses divided by earned premium; the core measure of underwriting profitability.
Business use: Headline KPI watched by line of business/region/underwriting year; underperforming = above target or worse than peer benchmark.

Definition: Loss ratio plus expense ratio; below 100% means underwriting at a profit.
Business use: The profitability read loss ratio alone misses — includes commission and operating expense.

Definition: Paid loss plus case reserves before recoveries; the ultimate expected cost of a claim.
Business use: Numerator of the loss ratio; the basis of record for claims cost (not paid alone).

Definition: Written premium recognised as the policy term elapses; the loss-ratio denominator.
Business use: Correct loss-ratio denominator (earned not written) so ratios reflect exposure on risk.

Definition: Claim-level listing (paid/reserve/incurred/recovery) from the claims table.
Business use: Claim-by-claim source of truth for claims analytics and the loss-ratio numerator; basis for cause-of-loss analysis.

Definition: Claim count divided by policy count; how often claims occur.
Business use: Shows whether a rising loss ratio is driven by more claims (risk selection/terms).

Definition: Incurred loss divided by claim count; the average cost per claim.
Business use: Shows whether a rising loss ratio is driven by bigger claims (pricing/cat exposure).

Definition: Estimated unpaid amount on the open portion of a claim (0 when closed).
Business use: Open/unpaid part of incurred loss; drives reserve development and IBNR; explains post-report movement.
